chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah and Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar from Safwan from Muhammad ibn Hakim from al-Abd al-Salih (peace be upon him) said:

I said to him, 'What is the waiting period of a young woman who menstruates like others, whose husband divorces her, and her menstruation is lifted?' He said: 'Three months.' I said, 'May I be your ransom, if she marries after three months and it becomes clear after she enters upon her husband that she is pregnant?' He said: 'Far be it from that, O Ibn Hakim! The lifting of menstruation is of two types: either it is the spoiling of a menstruation, so the husbands are permissible for her and she is not pregnant, or if she is pregnant, it will become apparent within three months, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has made it a time in which the pregnancy becomes apparent.'

I said, 'If she is in doubt?' He said: 'Her waiting period is nine months.' I said, 'If she is in doubt after nine months?' He said: 'The pregnancy is nine months.' I said, 'So if she marries?' He said: 'She should be cautious for three months.' I said, 'If she is in doubt after three months?' He said: 'There is no doubt upon her; she may marry.'
ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period for a woman with irregular menstruation after divorce?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi details the jurisprudential ruling for a woman with irregular menstruation (mustahadha) whose period ceases after divorce, establishing a three-month waiting period (iddah) for remarriage. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that if pregnancy occurs, it will become apparent within these three months, distinguishing between cessation due to miscarriage (where she is free to remarry) and ongoing pregnancy. The dialogue further addresses scenarios of doubt (irtibab) after three or nine months, providing precise legal boundaries for when she is considered free from the waiting period.
